## Background

I studied at the University of Toronto before beginning my career in property and casualty (P&C) insurance. Over the next three and a half years, I worked with claims data, quantitative models, and analytical workflows used to evaluate risk and support Insurance valutaion. This experience gave me an appreciation for both the technical side of modelling and the importance of understanding how analytical results are used in real-world decisions.

## Why Data Science

Working with data and models made me increasingly curious about methods beyond the traditional actuarial methods or approaches I had been using. In particular, I became interested in machine learning, AI, and how better programming and automation can change the way analytical work is performed. I joined UBC's Master of Data Science program to develop these capabilities more systematically, from statistical and advanced machine-learning methods to programming, data workflows, and collaborative software development practices.

## What I Want to Build

I am particularly interested in moving beyond simply using AI tools toward understanding how to build reliable AI-enabled analytical workflows. I want to become better at developing and validating modelling pipelines, automating repetitive analytical processes, and applying stronger software-engineering practices from data science. Over time, I hope to combine these skills with my industry experience to build tools and models that are both technically sound and applicable in practice.
